fixtures.source: Generated for picasu, not taken from an upstream project. ImageMagick writes the pixels and ExifTool writes the IIM record; neither writes an XMP packet, which is what makes the file an IIM-only case. Exact commands, run from the repository root: `magick -size 48x32 gradient:'#204060-#c0d0e0' -strip -quality 92 utils/snapfab/fixtures/jpeg/picasu-jpeg-48x32-iptc.jpg` followed by `exiftool -overwrite_original -q -IPTC:ObjectName='An IIM-only object name' -IPTC:Caption-Abstract='An IIM-only caption' -IPTC:Keywords=e2e_jpeg_iptc_alpine -IPTC:Keywords=e2e_jpeg_iptc_winter -IPTC:By-line='A. Fixture' -IPTC:City=Fixtureville -IPTC:CopyrightNotice='(c) 2024 picasu test fixtures' utils/snapfab/fixtures/jpeg/picasu-jpeg-48x32-iptc.jpg`. Re-running both reproduces the recorded SHA-256 exactly. `-strip` keeps an EXIF block out, and ExifTool's JPEG writer adds only the APP13 Photoshop image-resource block holding the IIM record (8BIM resource 0x0404): there is no APP1 XMP block and no `<?xpacket?>` markup anywhere in the file, which is the property the `iptc: [embedded]` claim is about.
fixtures.version: picasu fixture revision 1; ImageMagick 7.1.2-18 Q16 x86_64 23822 and ExifTool 13.59 (pure Perl)
fixtures.license: MIT (picasu repository LICENSE); no ImageMagick or ExifTool code is redistributed, only its output

expectedMetadata.xmp: none; the file carries no XMP packet, so the IIM record is its only metadata source
expectedMetadata.exif: none; the file carries no EXIF block, so the API returns an empty exifVec for it

fixtures.source: Constructed for picasu, not taken from upstream: a 48x32 8-bit RGB PNG written chunk by chunk by the script checked in beside it, so no image encoder was involved and the bytes depend only on that script and the Python standard library. Exact command, run from the repository root: `python3 utils/snapfab/fixtures/png/generate_picasu-png-48x32-xmp-text.py utils/snapfab/fixtures/png/picasu-png-48x32-xmp-text.png`. Re-running it reproduces the recorded SHA-256 byte for byte. Pixels are the same buffer as the TIFF and WebP fixtures (R = x*255/47, G = y*255/31, B = 128). Chunk order is IHDR, three tEXt chunks (Description, Comment, Source), one iTXt chunk with the keyword `XML:com.adobe.xmp`, compression flag 1 and compression method 0, then IDAT and IEND. The packet is therefore deflate-compressed in the file: neither `<?xpacket` nor `dc:subject` appears in the bytes, and a reader has to inflate it. Why a script and not ExifTool, the tool that reads it: ExifTool 13.59 writes a PNG's XMP packet into an *uncompressed* iTXt chunk (measured: the compression flag after the keyword is 0) and writes no tEXt chunk of its own choosing, so it cannot produce the case the claim is about.
fixtures.version: picasu fixture revision 1; python3 3.14.4 with zlib 1.3.1, standard library only

expectedMetadata.XMP-dc:Subject: e2e_png_xmp_alpine, e2e_png_xmp_winter
expectedMetadata.XMP-dc:Title: A title from the compressed packet
expectedMetadata.XMP-dc:Description: A caption from the compressed packet
expectedMetadata.PNG:Description: A text chunk description, which the packet's own dc:description outranks
expectedMetadata.exif: none; the file carries no eXIf chunk, so the API returns an empty exifVec for it

fixtures.source: Constructed for picasu, not taken from upstream: a 48x32 uncompressed RGB classic TIFF written field by field (little-endian header, IFD0 plus an Exif sub-IFD, one strip, 72 dpi). Pixels are the formula R = x*255/47, G = y*255/31, B = 128. DateTime is 2024:05:06 07:08:09 in IFD0, and DateTimeOriginal/DateTimeDigitized carry the same stamp in the Exif sub-IFD. No image encoder was involved, so the bytes depend only on that description.
fixtures.version: picasu fixture revision 1; python3 3.14 standard library only

expectedMetadata.xmp: sidecar only; the file carries no XMP packet

fixtures.source: Constructed for picasu from the same 48x32 RGB buffer as the TIFF fixture (R = x*255/47, G = y*255/31, B = 128). The buffer is encoded losslessly into a VP8L bitstream and muxed as extended format: VP8X with the Exif flag set, an EXIF chunk holding the TIFF block of the TIFF fixture verbatim as a bare TIFF stream, then the VP8L chunk. That layout is what upstream kamadak-exif ships in its own tests/exif.webp, whose EXIF chunk likewise holds a bare TIFF block with no JPEG `Exif\0\0` identifier. The pixel data round-trips byte for byte.
fixtures.version: picasu fixture revision 1; VP8L bitstream from ImageMagick 7.1.2-18 (libwebp 1.5.0) via `magick -define webp:lossless=true -quality 100`

fixtures.source: Generated for picasu, not taken from an upstream project. One 48x32 solid-colour frame at 1 fps from the lavfi `color` source, H.264 High profile in an ISO-BMFF file, no audio. Exact command, run from the repository root: `ffmpeg -nostdin -hide_banner -loglevel error -y -f lavfi -i color=c=0x204060:s=48x32:r=1:d=1 -frames:v 1 -c:v libx264 -preset veryfast -crf 30 -pix_fmt yuv420p -map_metadata -1 -fflags +bitexact -flags:v +bitexact -f mp4 utils/snapfab/fixtures/mp4/picasu-mp4-48x32-ffprobe.mp4`. The bytes are pinned by `-frames:v 1` (fixed content), `-map_metadata -1` (no inherited tags), and `-fflags +bitexact -flags:v +bitexact` (no creation_time, no encoder string); re-running the command reproduces the recorded SHA-256 exactly. ffmpeg's `-metadata` was deliberately NOT used: it writes iTunes-style `udta`/`ilst` tags, not the Adobe XMP `uuid` box, so the file carries no XMP packet at all. No Adobe XMP `uuid` box (`uuid` + BE7ACFCB-97A9-42E8-9C71-999491E3AFAC) and no XMP markup is present, which is why `xmp:embedded` is recorded as unsupported rather than unclaimed-and-assumed.
fixtures.version: picasu fixture revision 1; ffmpeg 8.0.1-3ubuntu2 (ffprobe 8.0.1-3ubuntu2) with libx264, Ubuntu build
fixtures.license: MIT (picasu repository LICENSE); no ffmpeg code is redistributed, only its output

expectedMetadata.xmp: sidecar only; the file carries no uuid-box XMP packet
expectedMetadata.exif: none; the exifVec the API returns for a video is ffprobe output, not EXIF
